Rashi on Gittin 59a:10:1.hebrew: רומז ונרמז - מה שהוא רומז קיים, ומה שרומזין לו והוא מתרצה קיים:
Rashi on Gittin 59a:10:1.english: Signals and is signaled to - What he signals is valid, and what [others] signal to him and he consents [to it] is valid:

Rashi on Gittin 59a:10:2.english: Gesturing - with his hands and with his head:

Rashi on Gittin 59a:10:3.hebrew: קפיצה - עקימת שפתים, שנא' "קפצה פיה" (איוב ה׳:ט״ז), ואינו סימן ניכר כרמיזה:
Rashi on Gittin 59a:10:3.english: Kefitzah [lip movement] - Bending of the lips, as it is said, "shuts its mouth" (Job 5:16), and it is not as recognizable a sign as gesturing:

Rashi on Gittin 59a:10:4.english: In [the case of] movable property - if he sold movable property.

Rashi on Gittin 59a:11:1.hebrew: אבל בגיטין - דקיי"ל: חרש שנשא משנתחרש, אם רצה להוציא, יוציא; כשם שכנס ברמיזה, כך מוציא ברמיזה (יבמות דף קיב):
Rashi on Gittin 59a:11:1.english: But with regard to bills of divorce - for it is established for us [that] a deaf-mute who married after becoming a deaf-mute, if he wishes to divorce [his wife], he may divorce [her]; just as he married [her] through gestures, so too he divorces [her] through gestures (Yevamot 112).

Rashi on Gittin 59a:12:1.english: It is obvious, we learned "regarding movable property" - [this is] in the statement of Ben Beteira:

Rashi on Gittin 59a:12:2.hebrew: מהו דתימא אף במטלטלין - קאמר, וכ"ש בגיטין; דלא תימא: גיטין הוא דקילי, משום דבקפיצה כנס — בקפיצה יוציא, אבל מטלטלין שנפלו בירושה — לא, מש"ה תנן "מטלטלין":
Rashi on Gittin 59a:12:2.english: Lest you say, "even regarding movable property" - [i.e., that the Mishnah] is saying [this], and all the more so regarding bills of divorce — so that you would not say: bills of divorce are lenient, because [just as] he married [her] with lip movement, he divorces [her] with lip movement, whereas movable property that came [to him] as an inheritance [is] not [transferred this way]; therefore [the Mishnah] taught "movable property":

Rashi on Gittin 59a:12:3.hebrew: קמ"ל - רב נחמן: מטלטלין דוקא נקט בן בתירא, ולא בגיטין ובקרקעות — לא ברמיזה ולא בקפיצה — דהכא הוא, משום כדי חייו תקון רבנן, כדלקמן:
Rashi on Gittin 59a:12:3.english: He teaches us - Rav Nachman [teaches us that] Ben Beteira specifically spoke of movable property, and not bills of divorce or real estate — neither by gesturing nor by lip movements — because here [in the case of movable property], it was for [the sake of] his livelihood that the Rabbis instituted [this], as [explained] below:

Rashi on Gittin 59a:15:1.hebrew: משום כדי חייו - דאי לאו זביניה זבינא, לא מזבני ליה מזוני ולא זבני מיניה:
Rashi on Gittin 59a:15:1.english: For the sake of his livelihood - For if his transaction is not a [valid] transaction, they will not sell him food, nor will they buy from him:

Rashi on Gittin 59a:16:1.hebrew: ויאמר לאשר על המלתחה - ביהוא כתיב, ומשום רבי אבא בר יעקב משום ר' יוחנן נקט לה:
Rashi on Gittin 59a:16:1.english: And he said to him who was over the wardrobe - It is written concerning Jehu, and [the Gemara] cited it on account of [the earlier statement of] Rabbi Abba bar Yaakov in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:

Rashi on Gittin 59a:16:2.hebrew: דבר הנמלל ונמתח - בגדי פשתן הן, שחוטן נמתח ע"י מלילה, שמולל באצבעותיו כשהוא טווה:
Rashi on Gittin 59a:16:2.english: Something that is rubbed and stretched - They are linen garments, whose thread is stretched through rubbing, as one rubs [it] with his fingers when he spins:

Rashi on Gittin 59a:17:1.english: Bonyam ben Nunyam - [He] was a wealthy Israelite:

Rashi on Gittin 59a:17:2.english: Sivni and choms, salselah and malmala - [These are] four types of garments of fine and good linen:

Rashi on Gittin 59a:17:3.hebrew: כי אמגוזא ופלגי אמגוזא - טלית גדולה למידתו, וכשהוא מקפלה לא היתה יותר מאגוז וחצי:
Rashi on Gittin 59a:17:3.english: Like a nut and half a nut - [It was] a cloak large [enough] for his size, and when he folded it, it was no more than a nut and a half:

Rashi on Gittin 59a:18:1.english: And their mistake - [That] of young children:

Rashi on Gittin 59a:18:2.english: Up to how much - [does it] retract [i.e., is the sale reversed]:

Rashi on Gittin 59a:18:3.hebrew: עד שתות כגדול - עד שתות, קנה הקונה ומחזיר אונאה; יותר משתות, בטל מקח:
Rashi on Gittin 59a:18:3.english: Up to one-sixth, like an adult - Up to one-sixth, the buyer acquires [the item] and [one] returns the price discrepancy; [if it is] more than one-sixth, the sale is void:

Rashi on Gittin 59a:19:1.hebrew: מתנתו מאי - במטלטלין, משום כדי חייו הוא: זביני — אין, מתנה — לא; או דלמא מתנתו נמי מתנה, דעבדו ליה נייח נפשיה:
Rashi on Gittin 59a:19:1.english: What [is the halakha regarding] his gift - [With regard to] movable property, [since the enactment] is on account of his livelihood: buying and selling — yes, [but] a gift — no; or perhaps his gift is also a [valid] gift, because [people] do what pleases him [in return]:

Rashi on Gittin 59a:1:1.english: I was [present] at the counting of Rabbi - at that vote in which they enacted that whoever is first to take [possession] acquires [it]:

Rashi on Gittin 59a:1:2.hebrew: ומינאי דידי מנו ברישא - ממני שאלו תחלה בשורה כשהיינו יושבין, מה דעתי נוטה; והוא היה בינוני, לא מן הגדולים ולא מן הקטנים, ואני שמעתי שקטן שבהם היה:
Rashi on Gittin 59a:1:2.english: And from me myself they counted first - They asked me first, in the row as we were sitting, which way my opinion inclined. He was in the middle — neither among the greatest nor among the youngest — though I have heard that he was the youngest of them.

Rashi on Gittin 59a:20:1.english: They reversed it - The members of the academy erred and reversed the statements of one Master to the other:

Rashi on Gittin 59a:20:2.hebrew: ושדרו לקמיה דרב מרדכי - כמאן ס"ל:
Rashi on Gittin 59a:20:2.english: And they sent [it] before Rav Mordekhai - [To ask] like whom he holds:

Rashi on Gittin 59a:20:3.hebrew: זילו אמרו ליה לבר מר - לבנו של רבי, דרב מרדכי תלמידו של רב אשי היה בכמה מקומות, ובמס' סוטה (דף מו:) אמרי' גבי לויה: "תלמיד לרב אין לו שיעור, רב מרדכי אלויה לרב אשי" כו':
Rashi on Gittin 59a:20:3.english: Go, say to Bar Mar - [Meaning,] to the son of my master, for Rav Mordekhai was a disciple of Rav Ashi [as seen] in several places, and in Tractate Sotah (46b) we say regarding escorting [a traveler]: "A disciple [escorting] a master has no limit; Rav Mordekhai escorted Rav Ashi," etc.

Rashi on Gittin 59a:20:4.english: When the Master was standing - [this refers to] Rav Ashi:

Rashi on Gittin 59a:20:5.hebrew: אדרגא - סולם של עליית בהמ"ד:
Rashi on Gittin 59a:20:5.english: On the step - A ladder of the upper story of the study hall:

Rashi on Gittin 59a:21:1.hebrew: כהן קורא ראשון כו' - כי היכי דלא ליתו לאינצויי, תקינו להו רבנן האי סידרא, דכיון דתקנתא דרבנן היא, תו לא מצינן לשנויי ולמימר "אנא קרינא ברישא":
Rashi on Gittin 59a:21:1.english: A priest reads first, etc. - So that they do not come to quarrel, the Sages instituted this order for them, for since it is a rabbinic enactment, we can no longer change [it] and say, "I will read first":

Rashi on Gittin 59a:21:2.hebrew: מערבין בבית ישן - בני חצר שרגילין ליתן עירוב החצר בבית אחד, אין משנין את מקומן ליתנו בבית אחר, מפני דרכי שלום; ובגמ' מפרש לה:
Rashi on Gittin 59a:21:2.english: They make an eiruv in an old house - Residents of a courtyard who are accustomed to placing the courtyard eiruv in one [particular] house do not change their place to put it in another house, on account of the ways of peace; and in the Gemara it explains it:

Rashi on Gittin 59a:2:1.hebrew: מתחילין מן הגדול - כשעומדין למנין, לראות אם רוב מטמאין או רוב מטהרין:
Rashi on Gittin 59a:2:1.english: They begin with the greatest [scholar] - When they stand [to take] a vote to see whether the majority declare [it] impure or the majority declare [it] pure:

Rashi on Gittin 59a:2:2.hebrew: מן הצד - מן הקטנים, ולא מן הגדול; שלא ילמד חובה, והשאר נכנעין מפניו שלא לחלוק עליו, משום "לא תענה על רב" (שמות כג), ובדיני נפשות מוקמינן להאי קרא בפ"ק דסנהדרין (דף ב.), "לא כהטייתך לטובה" כו', ולא ילמדו זכות:
Rashi on Gittin 59a:2:2.english: From the side - From the junior [judges], and not from the most senior [judge], lest he argue for conviction and the rest [of the judges] defer to him so as not to disagree with him — because of [the verse], "You shall not speak up in a dispute [against the senior judge]" (Exodus 23[:2]), and we establish this verse [as referring] to capital cases in the first chapter of Sanhedrin (2a), "[Your inclining for bad is] not like your inclining for good..." — and [thus] they would not argue for acquittal.

Rashi on Gittin 59a:3:1.hebrew: דכולהו מנינייהו מן הצד מתחילין - משום "לא תענה על ריב", וכתיב חסר בלא יו"ד, ודרשינן: "לא תענה על רב" — לא תחלוק על מופלא שבבית דין; ולא מוקמי ליה לרישא דקרא בדיני נפשות בלבד, ואע"ג דסיפיה דקרא לא מיתוקם אלא בדיני נפשות: וולס:
Rashi on Gittin 59a:3:1.english: All of their countings would begin on the side - Because [of the verse], "You shall not speak up in a dispute [riv]" (Exodus 23:2), and it is written defective without a yod, so we expound [it as]: "You shall not speak up against the master [rav]" — [meaning,] do not disagree with the most distinguished [judge] of the court; and [in the school of Rabbi] they do not restrict the beginning of the verse to capital cases [alone], even though the end of the verse is established only regarding capital cases:

Rashi on Gittin 59a:4:1.hebrew: במקום אחד - שתהא תורתן וגדולתן של ישראל במקום אחד, שאין בישראל גדול בתורה ובעושר כמותו:
Rashi on Gittin 59a:4:1.english: In one place - [Meaning] that the Torah and greatness of Israel should be in one place, that there is no one in Israel as great in Torah and in wealth as he:

Rashi on Gittin 59a:5:1.english: And wasn't there Elazar - alone after Joshua passed away:

Rashi on Gittin 59a:5:2.hebrew: והא הוה פנחס - לאחר אלעזר, שהיו בו תורה וגדולה, שהיה כהן גדול אחר אביו:
Rashi on Gittin 59a:5:2.english: And wasn't there Pinchas - after Elazar, [who possessed] Torah and greatness, as he was High Priest after his father:

Rashi on Gittin 59a:5:3.hebrew: הוו זקנים - שקבלו מיהושע והאריכו ימים אחריו, כדכתיב (יהושע כ״ד:ל״א): "אשר האריכו ימים אחרי יהושע":
Rashi on Gittin 59a:5:3.english: There were the Elders - who received [the tradition] from Joshua and outlived him, as it is written (Joshua 24:31): "who outlived Joshua":

Rashi on Gittin 59a:6:1.hebrew: שאול - גדול בתורה היה, אלא שלא לימד לאחרים, כדאמרי' בעירובין (דף נג.): "שאול לא גלי מסכתא", להכי כתיב ביה: "בכל אשר יפנה ירשיע":
Rashi on Gittin 59a:6:1.english: Saul - He was great in Torah, except that he did not teach others, as we say in Eruvin (53a): "Saul did not reveal [his] tractate"; therefore it is written concerning him: "Wherever he turned, he would be found wrong":

Rashi on Gittin 59a:6:2.english: But didn't he pass away - [That is, the passing] of Samuel, before Saul:

Rashi on Gittin 59a:6:3.hebrew: כולהו שני - משעמד בגדולה תהא תורה וגדולה במקום אחד, וזה בתחילת גדולתו לא יחיד היה בתורה:
Rashi on Gittin 59a:6:3.english: All the years - [Meaning that] from when he assumed greatness, Torah and greatness must be in one place, and this one [Saul], at the beginning of his greatness, was not unique in Torah:

Rashi on Gittin 59a:6:4.hebrew: עירא היאירי - גדול בתורה היה, כדאמרינן במו"ק (דף טז:) דהוה מתני להו לרבנן על גבי כרים וכסתות:
Rashi on Gittin 59a:6:4.english: Ira the Jairite - He was great in Torah, as we say in Moed Katan (16b) that he used to teach the Rabbis [sitting] upon pillows and cushions:

Rashi on Gittin 59a:8:1.hebrew: חזקיה - מלך יהודה, גדול בתורה היה, כדאמרינן בחלק (סנהדרין דף צד:):
Rashi on Gittin 59a:8:1.english: Hezekiah - King of Judah, was great in Torah, as we say in [the chapter entitled] Chelek (Sanhedrin 94b):

Rashi on Gittin 59a:8:2.hebrew: שבנא - גדול בתורה היה, כדאמרינן בסנהדרין (כו.): שבנא הוה דריש בתליסר ריבוותא, וחזקיה בחד סרי ריבוותא:
Rashi on Gittin 59a:8:2.english: Shebnah - He was great in Torah, as we say in Sanhedrin (26a): Shebnah would lecture before thirteen myriads [of students], and Hezekiah before eleven myriads:

Rashi on Gittin 59a:8:3.hebrew: והא איקטיל - סנחריב הרגו, כדאמרינן בזה בורר (שם):
Rashi on Gittin 59a:8:3.english: And wasn't he killed - Sennacherib killed him, as we say in [the chapter] Zeh Borer (there):

Tosafot on Gittin 59a:20:1.hebrew: אחת מתנה מרובה ואחת מתנה מועטת - ומדלא קאמר נמי "אחת מתנת מטלטלין ואחת קרקעות", נראה דוקא במטלטלין דאיירי בהו קאמר. והא דאמרי' במי שמת (ב"ב דף) קנה:) גבי פחות מבן כ', דאין מוכר בנכסי אביו ומתנתו מתנה במקרקעי — התם בגדול, שהוא בן י"ג שנים ויום אחד, אלא דלא היה בן עשרים:
Tosafot on Gittin 59a:20:1.english: Whether a large gift or a small gift - And from [the fact] that he did not also say "whether a gift of movable property or [a gift of] real estate," it appears that he is speaking specifically about movable property, which they were discussing. And [as for] that which we say in [the chapter entitled] Mi Shemet (Bava Batra 155b) regarding one who is under twenty [years old], that he cannot sell his father's property yet his gift is a valid gift [even] with respect to real estate — there [it is speaking] of an adult, who is thirteen years and one day old, except that he was not yet twenty [years old]:

Tosafot on Gittin 59a:3:1.hebrew: דכולהו מנינייהו מן הצד הוו מתחלי - פי' בקונט' דמוקי לה "לא תענה על ריב" בכל דבר, ואין נראה, דלא מיסתבר דפליג אמתניתין דסנהדרין (דף לב.) דאייתי; אלא משום ענוה, שלא להראות עצמו גדול היה עושה:
Tosafot on Gittin 59a:3:1.english: All of their countings would begin from the side - Rashi explained that [Rabbi] applies "You shall not respond in a dispute" to every matter. But this does not seem [correct], for it is not reasonable that he disagrees with the Mishnah in Sanhedrin (32a) that [the Gemara] cited; rather, he would do [this] out of humility, so as not to show himself [to be] great:

Tosafot on Gittin 59a:9:1.hebrew: והא הוה הונא בר נתן - תורה וגדולה היתה לו, כדאמרינן במו"ק (דף כח.) דקא דחקא רגלי דהונא בר נתן; ואמר בפ' ב' דזבחים (דף יט.) דאיקיים ביה "והיו מלכים אומניך":
Tosafot on Gittin 59a:9:1.english: But wasn’t there Huna bar Natan - He had [both] Torah [scholarship] and greatness, as [the Gemara] says in Moed Katan (28a), that the feet of Huna bar Natan were pressing [to succeed Rav Ashi]; and [the Gemara] says in the second chapter of Zevachim (19a) that [the verse] "And kings shall be your foster fathers" was fulfilled in him:
